seo.title: Homeless help in Los Angeles - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Los Angeles: shelter, meals, health care, jobs, ID, benefits, and legal help.

page.heading: Los Angeles homeless and housing-crisis help

notice.text: Beds, schedules, routes, and eligibility can change.
Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, money, or job the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.

content.text: When asking for help, give your exact location or nearest landmark, whether you have a safe place tonight, when you last ate, medical needs, age, pregnancy or disability, children or pets with you, and whether you have identification. Ask the worker to explain the next step, required documents, transportation, and what to do if no bed is open.

adults and young people seeking a bed can call 800-548-6047; households with a child under 18 should call 211. A Coordinated Entry access center can also assess housing needs. Shelter placement is based on eligibility and availability.
. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly.
immediate violence, serious injury, trouble breathing, loss of consciousness, fire, overdose, or another life-threatening emergency. Give a precise location and describe the danger first.
City of Los Angeles homeless-services guidance
adult shelter and shelter for youth ages 16–24. Tell the operator your age, household, location, health or mobility needs, pets, and whether you need transportation.
family shelter, food, benefits, health, legal, domestic-violence, and other local referrals. Ask the operator to check current eligibility and hours rather than relying on an old address.
mental-health and substance-use referrals, crisis assessment, field response, interpretation, and transportation when appropriate. Call 911 if there is immediate physical danger.
LA County Department of Mental Health — get help now
assessment and connection to emergency, interim, and permanent-housing programs. An assessment is not a promise of immediate housing; keep your contact details current with the caseworker.
545 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013
single adults and several family types. The published intake requires proof of ID and a Megan's Law clearance; call first if you lack ID.
; men's intake extension 309, women's intake extension 518.
emergency services, recovery-oriented residential programs, meals, showers, clothing, classes, and employment help. Call for current bed and intake rules.
601 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014
shelter and supportive services for single men and women, emergency food, personal goods, housing help, and recovery programs. Confirm current intake before arrival.

content.text: 6:30 p.m., first come, first served; the door sign states that night's available beds.
a brief Christian service, dinner, shower, bed, and breakfast. Because capacity is limited, also call the LAHSA shelter line rather than relying on one location.
1325 N. Western Avenue, Los Angeles, CA 90027
; emergency services are open 24 hours and walk-ins are accepted.
free emergency shelter, meals, showers, clothing, health care, education, employment, transportation, and case management for young adults, including LGBTQ+ youth.
use the LAHSA safe-parking list or call 211.
legal overnight parking for people living in a vehicle; city-listed sites have restrooms and security. Registration, vehicle documents, hours, and rules vary by lot.
City of Los Angeles — Safe Parking programs
safety planning and connection to confidential emergency shelter and longer-term housing for survivors and children. Call 911 if the danger is immediate.
breakfast 5:30 a.m., lunch 12:30 p.m., and dinner 6:45 p.m. Meals, showers, and clothing are among the emergency services; confirm the daily line and any changes.
Los Angeles Mission meal and service information

items.name: Union Rescue Mission — meals and hygiene

content.text: three meals daily for guests, showers, haircuts, clothing, and laundry. Community access and intake rules can differ from resident services, so call first.

items.name: The Midnight Mission — meals and restrooms

content.text: . The organization provides emergency food and personal goods; a current county listing confirms weekday service. Call for today's meal and shower times.

items.name: Hospitality Kitchen — Los Angeles Catholic Worker

content.text: food Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, 7:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. Confirm the current schedule before making a long trip.

items.name: Bee a Little Better — Thursday meal

content.text: Union Church parking lot, 401 E. 3rd Street
hot meals, water, toiletries, first-aid supplies, and donated seasonal items. Outdoor distribution can be canceled or moved, so check the organization first.
current referrals to food pantries and meal programs across Los Angeles County. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask whether ID, proof of address, or an appointment is required.
Christian mission offering shelter, meals, hygiene, medical, dental, legal, mental-health, recovery, and family services. Some programs require ID and screening.
meals, showers, clothing, recovery, education, employment workshops, job-search help, psychiatric referrals, and a free legal clinic.
secular homeless services including shelter, food, housing help, personal goods, recovery, and education. Ask intake which services are available without a shelter placement.

items.name: Los Angeles Public Library homeless resources

content.text: local libraries can connect people to jobs, food, housing, computers, and other support. Ask 311 or the library system for the closest branch and current social-service schedule.
overdose, unconsciousness, serious injury, severe breathing trouble, chest pain, heavy bleeding, or another life-threatening condition. Do not delay because of insurance or ID concerns.
522 S. San Pedro Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013
community health clinic serving people in and around Skid Row, including medical outreach and HIV and STI testing and treatment. Call for current hours, cost, and walk-in rules.
mental-health and substance-use support, screening, referrals, crisis assessment, field response, interpretation, and transport. Ask specifically for homeless outreach if needed.
information and connection to substance-use treatment in Los Angeles County. Tell the operator if you have no phone, transportation, insurance, or safe place to stay.
LA County crisis and service lines
URM publishes medical, dental, legal, and mental-health care for guests; LA Mission offers psychiatric referrals. Ask what is available to a person not yet admitted.
referrals for food, shelter, health, financial support, legal help, and county programs. Ask for the correct benefits office and the documents needed for CalFresh or other aid.
request non-emergency outreach for a person living outside. Provide a precise, publicly accessible location and useful description. Do not use it for immediate danger; call 911 instead.
LAPD homeless-services FAQ and LA-HOP guidance
city information and non-emergency service requests. For shelter placement call 800-548-6047 or 211; for outreach, ask for LA-HOP.

items.name: Housing help through a county clinic

content.text: county Health Services can connect patients to clinics and housing resources, including Coordinated Entry, shelter, safe parking, domestic-violence shelter, and eviction prevention.
LA County Health Services — housing resources
the City network provides job-readiness workshops, training, job search, and employer connections, including services for people experiencing homelessness.
use the official center list or ask 311 for the nearest active WorkSource Center; confirm ID and appointment requirements.
employment-readiness workshops, job-search assistance, GED preparation, computer skills, ESL, vocational training, and referrals. Intake depends on the service or residential program.

items.name: Covenant House — work and education for ages 18–24

content.text: education enrollment, tutoring, GED, ESL, employment services, case management, and transportation for young adults in its programs.
free help for eligible people with license reinstatement, unpaid tickets, unemployment benefits, credit, and criminal-record clearing. A shelter or housing worker can also send a referral.
a person meeting the federal definition of homelessness may qualify for a no-fee California identification card.
ask a government agency or qualifying nonprofit serving unhoused people to verify your status and issue the DMV verification form before visiting DMV.

a qualified provider issues the no-fee verification. For a REAL ID, an applicant may use the verification plus a letter from a shelter, nonprofit, faith organization, employer, or government agency attesting California residence.
a Coordinated Entry caseworker, mission, or public-benefits office whether it is registered to issue the form.

items.name: ID help through a shelter or caseworker

content.text: identity-document replacement, a mailing address, fee-verification form, and help obtaining birth records. Keep copies and receipts separate from original documents.
free help for eligible people experiencing or nearing homelessness with housing, benefits, family law, restraining orders, tickets, license reinstatement, credit, and record clearing.
helps people experiencing homelessness resolve eligible bench warrants, misdemeanor cases, citations, fines, fees, and convictions, and connects participants to housing and job support.
ask a homeless-services caseworker for a current referral and court location; eligibility differs by case.
LA County Public Defender — Community Outreach Courts

items.name: Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles

content.text: free help for eligible low-income residents with housing, benefits, immigration, family, and record-clearing matters. Representation depends on the case and capacity.
207 S. Broadway, 6th floor, Los Angeles, CA 90012
pre-eviction, eviction, notices to vacate, court preparation, and housing advice. The 2026 city bulletin lists weekday walk-in, first-come service; confirm before visiting.
Los Angeles Housing Department legal referrals
safety planning, emergency-shelter referrals, counseling, housing, and legal resources for survivors and children. Use a safe phone when possible; call 911 for immediate danger.
English and Spanish crisis support, safety planning, referrals, and information about intake availability for a 45-day emergency shelter. Other languages can be arranged.
ages 18–24, including young people at risk of trafficking and LGBTQ+ youth. Walk-in emergency shelter and services are free.
suspected abuse or neglect of a child in Los Angeles County. Call 911 if a child is in immediate danger or needs emergency medical care.
forced labor, commercial sexual exploitation, withheld ID, threats, or inability to leave. Do not confront a suspected exploiter; call 911 if danger is immediate.
